evidence: mobile-native/androidApp/src/main/java/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/navigation/Navigation.kt:493 — the CreateListing composable route wires onSubmit to `Result.failure(NotImplementedError("Wire to listing API"))`, so the realtor 'Create Listing' feature ALWAYS fails in production. Reachable from the MyListings screen's onCreateClick FAB (Navigation.kt:483) → Screen.CreateListing.route.

mobile-native/androidApp/src/main/java/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/ui/realtor/CreateListingScreen.kt:39-135 — a full 399-line form (title/description/city/price/currency/transactionType OutlinedTextFields + validation + submit button) collects CreateListingInput and calls `onSubmit(...)`; on the hardwired failure it shows R.string.realtor_create_validation_publish_failed. A user fills the entire form, taps Publish, and is told publishing failed every time.

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/realtor/PortalListingsRepository.kt:40-145 — the repository exposes only listMyListings / getListingAnalytics / getPortfolioAnalytics; there is NO create method at all. The submit callback has nothing to call. Landable fix: add `suspend fun createListing(input): Result<Unit>` (POST /api/v1/my/listings) and wire it into the Navigation.kt route in place of the NotImplementedError.

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/realtor/PortalListingsRepository.kt:111-124 — getPortfolioAnalytics() fans out one getListingAnalytics HTTP call per listing via `listings.map { async { ... } }.awaitAll()` with NO concurrency cap. listMyListings(limit = 100) means up to 100 simultaneous GET /api/v1/my/listings/{id}/analytics requests fired at once from a mobile Ktor client.

On mobile this can exhaust the Ktor HttpClient connection pool, trigger server-side rate limiting (all 100 hit the same host in one burst), and spike radio/battery for a realtor with a large portfolio. The comment acknowledges the fan-out is intentional but sets no bound.

Landable fix: bound concurrency (e.g. `listings.chunked(8)` sequential batches, or a `Semaphore(8)` around each async) so the dashboard load degrades gracefully instead of issuing an unbounded request burst. Covered by the existing PortalListingsRepositoryTest.kt harness.
